Alcohol A direct relationship between alcohol use and blood pressure has been well documented. 
This effect is particularly evident with alcohol intakes of more than 2 drinks per day (a drink is 
defined as 12 ounces beer, 5 ounces wine, or 1.5 ounces spirits). A meta-analysis of 15 randomly 
controlled trials found that reduction of alcohol intake resulted in a decrease in SBP of 3.3 mm Hg 
and DBP of 2.0 mm Hg. It was also found that the greater the reduction in alcohol intake, the greater 
the reduction of BP. From these studies it was suggested that for each reduction of one alcoholic 
drink per day, a reduction in both systolic and DBP of 1 mm Hg resulted.
